what: The first fine-tuning run driven end to end on native Windows: created, trained, delivered, RETRIEVED over the Windows-safe HTTP path, acknowledged on-chain, and minted into a Model Passport carrying a REAL adapter root and an EARNED attestation flag.
why: Run 1 lost its model at acknowledgement on Windows (ENOENT + 429). Run 2 recovered only by moving to WSL2 Linux. Run 3 proved the daemon on Linux. None of them was a complete, honest end-to-end fine-tune on native win32 that ended in a minted passport with an on-chain-verified adapter. This run is that: the DEFECT-01 HttpModelRetriever downloaded the 93 MB artifact on this Windows host and re-derived its 0G Storage root to match the on-chain model root before anything was acknowledged.

driver.retrieved_by: tools/run4-retrieve.mts — services/orchestrator/src/retrieval.ts HttpModelRetriever, with a curl streaming+resume fetchImpl (transport hardening only; validation unchanged)
driver.minted_by: tools/run4-mint.mts (@crucible/core buildManifest + isVerifiedAdapterRoot; ethers mint against Passport.sol; @0gfoundation/0g-storage-ts-sdk upload)

preflight.note: Ledger and fine-tuning sub-account already existed and were funded from prior runs; nothing needed funding. Landmine #4 (false 3 0G addLedger guard) avoided.

configuration.datasetFile: datasets/sentiment/train.jsonl (resolved by tools/identify-dataset.mjs — the chain-anchored root is authoritative over any path note)
configuration.note: Dataset REUSED at its existing 0G Storage root — no upload, avoiding landmine #1 (Windows uploadDataset spawns a Linux ELF).

timeline.task_created: 2026-09-18T04:42Z (approx; createTask is a provider-API call, not a wallet tx)
timeline.note: Delivered ~4 min after SettingUp. Acknowledged ~6 min after delivery (promptly — landmine #3), well inside the 48h window and before the provider's ~6h settlement.

retrieval.transport: HTTP GET {indexer}/file?root=<modelRootHash>, streamed to disk by curl with resume (-C -) and retry
retrieval.note: The exact failure the coordinator warned about occurred: the first curl attempt died mid-stream at 61,351,230 bytes (schannel 'server closed abruptly'). Resume + retry completed the full 93,642,471 bytes on the second attempt. HttpModelRetriever then recomputed the 0G Storage Merkle root (storage-hash.ts zgStorageRoot) and it matched the on-chain model root EXACTLY before anything was acknowledged. Do NOT use the SDK 'auto' download (landmine #2) — this is the Windows-safe path.

deliverable.note: acknowledged=true read back from FineTuningServing.getDeliverables — the chain is authoritative, not the provider status text. encryptedSecret filled to 129 bytes once the provider settled.

dataset.tokenCountDerivation: settled task fee 11852800000000000 neuron / price 800000000000 neuron-per-token = 14816 tokens (checkable)

fee.chargedTo: fine-tuning sub-account (compute ledger), not the wallet
fee.note: Identical to runs 1-3 on the same dataset/config. Charged against the sub-account; the wallet paid only gas + the storage-upload fee.

passport.note: First Crucible passport with adapter.hashSource='onchain-verified' AND tee.attestationVerified=true. The adapter root was read off the chain and independently retrieved+validated on win32; the attestation flag is earned by runs/attestation-testnet.json (verifyService passed: signer + compose match).

strangerVerification.note: Downloaded the manifest back from 0G Storage by root hash, hashed the exact bytes, and verifyManifest(3, that hash) returned true on-chain — checkable by anyone with no wallet and no clone of this repo.

cost.walletDeltaNote: gas for acknowledge + mint + the storage-upload transaction. The 0.0118528 0G training fee is debited from the compute sub-account, not the wallet.

whatThisProves: The DEFECT-01 HttpModelRetriever completes a real ~93 MB model download on native Windows and validates it against the on-chain root — the retrieval that ENOENTed and cost run 1 its model.
A delivered deliverable can be acknowledged on-chain on Windows via acknowledgeDeliverable AFTER an out-of-band validated HTTP retrieval, avoiding the broken SDK acknowledgeModel download path.
A Model Passport can carry a genuinely on-chain-verified adapter root plus an earned attestationVerified=true, and its manifest lives on 0G Storage where a stranger can verify it end to end.
whatThisDoesNotProve: That the provider trained honestly on the dataset. Crucible proves lineage, not honest training — a provider returning arbitrary weights would produce a passport that verifies the same way.
That the SDK's own acknowledgeModel download works on Windows. It does not; this run deliberately routed around it (landmine #2).
